AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).

For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).

<span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />

## Version-matched documentation

Next.js 16.2 and later include documentation that matches the installed framework version. The documentation is available at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and mirrors the structure of the [Next.js documentation site](https://nextjs.org/docs):

```txt
node_modules/next/dist/docs/
├── 01-app/
│   ├── 01-getting-started/
│   ├── 02-guides/
│   └── 03-api-reference/
├── 02-pages/
├── 03-architecture/
└── index.mdx
```

The bundled copy gives coding agents access to the APIs and patterns supported by the project without a network request or external lookup. [Upgrading Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/upgrading) also updates the bundled documentation.

### Managed documentation instructions

Next.js makes the bundled documentation discoverable through managed instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the project root. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot read this file when they start a session.

[`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) creates the agent files for new projects. When `next dev` detects a coding agent, it creates or updates the managed instructions for existing projects. The block directs the agent to the documentation installed with the project:

```md filename="AGENTS.md"
<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->

## This is NOT the Next.js you know

This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.

This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.

<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
```

Next.js updates only the content between the agent rules markers and preserves the rest of `AGENTS.md`.

[Research comparing `AGENTS.md` with knowledge Skills](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals) found a 100% pass rate with bundled documentation, compared with up to 79% for Skill-based approaches. See the current [Next.js agent evaluation results](https://nextjs.org/evals).

Managed documentation instructions are enabled by default in Next.js 16.3 and later. See the [`agentRules` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules) to configure or disable them.

### Version support

Next.js 16.3 and later include bundled documentation and support managed agent instructions. Next.js 16.2 includes the bundled documentation but does not generate instructions automatically.

Next.js 16.1 and earlier do not include the bundled documentation. The legacy `agents-md` command downloads a version-matched copy to `.next-docs/` and indexes it in `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
```

### Docs over the network

The Next.js documentation is also available as Markdown over the network for agents that fetch pages instead of reading `node_modules`. Every page on [nextjs.org/docs](https://nextjs.org/docs) has a plain Markdown version at its `.md` URL, and clients that send an `Accept: text/markdown` header receive Markdown. This includes the per-error pages under `/docs/messages`, which are not bundled.

The index at [`/docs/llms.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt) and the single-file [`/docs/llms-full.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms-full.txt) follow the [`llms.txt` convention](https://llmstxt.org/), so agents that already read `llms.txt` for other tools can discover the Next.js docs the same way.

### Controlling return values

Server Action return values are serialized and sent to the client. Only return what the UI needs, not raw database records.

```tsx filename="app/actions.ts"
'use server'

import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
import { db } from '@/lib/db'

// BAD: Returns the full database record, which may include
// internal fields the client should not see.
export async function updateUser(data: FormData) {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session?.user) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
  }
  return db.user.update({
    where: { id: session.user.id },
    data: { name: data.get('name') as string },
  })
}

// GOOD: Returns only what the client needs.
export async function updateUserSafe(data: FormData) {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session?.user) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
  }
  await db.user.update({
    where: { id: session.user.id },
    data: { name: data.get('name') as string },
  })
  return { success: true }
}
```

### Rate limiting

For expensive operations (sending emails, writing to a database), consider adding rate limiting to prevent abuse. See the [Rate limiting](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#rate-limiting) example in the Backend for Frontend guide.

### Closures and encryption

Defining a Server Action inside a component creates a [closure](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Closures) where the action has access to the outer function's scope. For example, the `publish` action has access to the `publishVersion` variable:

    }

Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching):

```ts filename="next.config.ts"
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
  partialPrefetching: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.

# SignalScout AI: plan for `src/core/agent/` and `src/app/`

I didn't modify any files or run any Git commands. I read the repository and the Next.js 16.4.0 docs bundled in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`.

## Starting point

- **App:** `src/app/` still holds the default create-next-app files: [layout.tsx](src/app/layout.tsx) with "Create Next App" metadata and a boilerplate [page.tsx](src/app/page.tsx).
- **Core and tests:** `src/core/{agent,data,fixtures,observability}`, `tests/` and `scripts/` contain only `.gitkeep`. `src/core/types.ts` doesn't exist yet.
- **Credentials:** `.env` has one variable, `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY`, so Crustdata is the paid enrichment provider. No LLM SDK or key is installed.
- **Dependencies:** `zod` is present but only because something else depends on it; it isn't in `package.json`. `server-only` isn't installed either (Next handles that import internally). There's no `vitest.config`, and Cache Components isn't turned on.

## 1. Modules in `src/core/agent/`

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `index.ts` | The public entry point. Exports `runPipeline` and nothing internal. |
| `pipeline.ts` | Runs the stages in order and emits a `StageEvent` for each. Records a failure in one stage without crashing the run, and builds the `RunResult`. |
| `icp.ts` | Checks and cleans up the ideal customer profile (ICP) input, then turns it into search filters and scoring criteria. |
| `source.ts` | Fetches candidate prospects through the `ProspectSource` interface (fixture data, Crustdata search or CSV) and tags where each came from. |
| `validate.ts` | Free, deterministic checks: required fields, domain format, duplicates, exclusion lists, location and company-size limits. Gives each prospect a quick fit score from data we already have. |
| `budget.ts` | `EnrichmentBudget`: limits calls per run, guarantees one call per unique domain, limits concurrency, and counts what was spent. Pure code, so it's easy to test. |
| `enrich.ts` | Controlled enrichment: picks the best validated prospects, checks the cache, then calls the provider through the budget. A failed call is recorded and doesn't stop the run. |
| `score.ts` | Deterministic weighted scoring. Produces a 0–100 score, a tier, a per-criterion breakdown with evidence, and a confidence level (lower when a prospect wasn't enriched). |
| `outreach.ts` | Writes drafts for qualified prospects only, behind an `OutreachWriter` interface. Defaults to templates. A draft may only mention facts that are in the prospect record. Nothing is sent. |
| `config.ts` | Default thresholds, weights, limits and the server's maximum budget. |

**Rules for the core:**
- Every external service is passed in as a dependency: source, enrichment provider, cache, writer, observer, clock and ID generator.
- The core never reads `process.env` and never imports `server-only`. Both rules keep it importable in Vitest without a network. This also follows the docs' advice to keep secret access inside a dedicated data-access layer.

## 2. Pipeline stages

1. **ICP intake.** Turn the raw form data into a clean ICP. Invalid fields return field-level errors before any work starts.
2. **Sourcing.** Fetch up to `maxProspects` candidates. A paid search call is charged to the same budget.
3. **Validation.** Each prospect is marked `valid` or `rejected`, with reason codes. Duplicates are found by a normalized key (domain without `www.`, lowercase).
4. **Controlled enrichment.** Rank valid prospects by quick fit score, enrich only the top K above a threshold, and mark the rest `skipped_low_fit` or `skipped_budget`.
5. **Scoring.** Score everyone who passed validation and assign tiers A, B, C or disqualified.
6. **Outreach.** Write drafts for tiers A and B only, up to N drafts.
7. **Result assembly.** Collect the outputs plus stats (counts per stage, calls used, cache hits, skips, time taken) and warnings.

## 3. Pages and components in `src/app/`

Following the docs' private-folder convention, `_components` is not a route.

- **`layout.tsx`:** change the metadata to SignalScout AI.
- **`page.tsx`:** a Server Component that holds the form and the results area. It sets `export const maxDuration = 60`; the docs say a page-level `maxDuration` applies to every Server Action on that page.
- **`actions.ts`:** marked `'use server'` and `import 'server-only'`. Defines `runSignalScout(prevState, formData)`.
- **`error.tsx`:** catches unexpected errors.
- **`_components/`:**
  - `IcpForm` (client component): uses `useActionState` for the pending state and field errors, has a synthetic-data toggle, and disables submit while a run is in progress.
  - `RunSummary`: the funnel counts and budget meter (used, saved by cache, skipped).
  - `ProspectTable`: tier, score and status per prospect, with expandable rows.
  - `ScoreBreakdown`: the per-criterion score, with evidence.
  - `OutreachDraft` (client component): shows a draft with a copy button.
  - `StageTimeline`: each stage's status and timing, and the reasons prospects were rejected.
- **`_lib/`:**
  - `parseIcpForm.ts`: turns `FormData` into `IcpInput`. Pure code, so it's testable.
  - `toRunView.ts`: trims `RunResult` down to what the client needs.
  - `deps.ts`: server-only. Builds either the real or the synthetic dependencies.

**Later:** a `/runs/[id]` page needs a place to store runs, and live progress needs a streaming Route Handler (see section 4).

## 4. How the UI calls the pipeline

1. `IcpForm` → `useActionState(runSignalScout)`
2. `runSignalScout` runs `parseIcpForm` and validates on the server. The docs say Server Action input must be validated there. If the input is invalid, it returns `{ fieldErrors }`.
3. It clamps the requested budget to the server's maximum.
4. It calls `deps.ts`, which picks fixture providers or Crustdata providers.
5. It runs `runPipeline(icp, deps, { budget, signal })`.
6. It returns `toRunView(result)`: a serializable, trimmed view.

**Why this design:**
- The docs say to return only what the UI needs from a Server Action, so raw provider payloads never reach the browser.
- Server Actions are queued and handled one at a time. That's fine for one run per submit, but it rules out parallel fetching through actions. Any parallel work belongs inside the pipeline.
- I'm not proposing `use cache` or Cache Components for runs. Each run is a user-triggered action, and the docs note that in-memory caching doesn't persist between serverless requests. Enrichment caching belongs behind a cache interface instead.
- **Stretch goal:** a `POST app/api/runs/route.ts` that streams stage events as a `ReadableStream` (the docs show this pattern), to show live progress.

## 5. Types my teammate needs to define in `src/core/types.ts`

**Input:**
- `IcpInput`: the raw form fields — industries, employee range, locations, target titles and seniority, keywords, excluded domains, `maxProspects`, `enrichmentBudget`, `useSyntheticData`.
- `NormalizedIcp`: the cleaned version.

**Prospects:**
- `Prospect`: `id`, `dedupeKey`, company fields (name, domain, industry, employee count, country, LinkedIn URL), an optional contact (name, title, seniority), and `source`.

**Validation:**
- `ValidationIssue`: `{ code, message, field? }`, where `code` is a fixed set of values.
- `ValidationResult`: `{ prospectId, status: 'valid' | 'rejected', issues }`.

**Enrichment:**
- `Signal`: `{ type, description, date?, sourceUrl? }`.
- `EnrichmentData`: headcount growth, funding stage and date, tech stack, hiring activity, `signals[]`.
- `EnrichmentResult`: `{ prospectId, status: 'enriched' | 'cached' | 'skipped_budget' | 'skipped_low_fit' | 'failed', data?, error?, costUnits }`.

**Scoring:**
- `ScoreComponent`: `{ criterion, weight, value, points, evidence }`.
- `ScoredProspect`: `{ prospect, enrichment?, score, tier, breakdown, confidence }`.

**Outreach:**
- `OutreachDraft`: `{ prospectId, channel, subject, body, factsUsed[] }`.

**Runs:**
- `PipelineStage` (one value per stage), `StageEvent`, `RunStats`, `RunResult`.

**Interfaces my code calls and my teammate implements:**
- `ProspectSource.search(icp, { limit, signal })`
- `EnrichmentProvider.enrich(prospect, { signal })`
- `EnrichmentCache` with `get` and `set`
- `PipelineObserver.onEvent(event)`
- `OutreachWriter`

## 6. Limiting enrichment calls and API costs

1. **Free checks first.** Validation and duplicate removal happen before any paid call, and rejected prospects are never enriched.
2. **Enrich only the top K.** K is the smallest of the user's budget, the server's maximum and the number of prospects above the quick-fit threshold.
3. **A hard budget.** `budget.ts` checks before every call, and search calls count too. When it runs out, the rest are marked `skipped_budget`; nothing throws. The server clamps whatever budget the user enters.
4. **One call per domain per run, plus a cache.** Cache hits cost nothing and are counted separately.
5. **Concurrency limit and timeouts.** Roughly 3 calls at once, each with a timeout passed as an `AbortSignal`. At most one retry, only on a rate-limit (429) or server (5xx) error, and the retry counts against the budget.
6. **Synthetic data by default.** Dev and tests use the fixture provider. The real provider is used only when the user turns off synthetic data and the API key exists.
7. **Request only the fields scoring uses**, if Crustdata supports choosing fields.
8. **No double submits.** The button is disabled while pending, and the server allows one run at a time per process. The docs also suggest rate-limiting expensive operations.
9. **Show the spend.** `RunSummary` displays calls used, saved and skipped.

## 7. Testing with synthetic fixtures

**Suggested fixtures** (my teammate owns the fixtures folder): an ICP plus a mixed prospect set, covering:
- a perfect fit
- duplicate domains differing only by `www.` or capitalization
- a missing or malformed domain
- an excluded domain
- the wrong location
- too small or too large
- a provider failure
- an empty enrichment result

**Fake providers:**
- `FakeEnrichmentProvider` counts its calls and can be set to fail or return a rate-limit error for chosen domains.
- An in-memory cache.
- A fixed clock and ID generator, so test output is stable.

**What the tests check:**
- **ICP input:** invalid input produces field errors.
- **Validation:** the right reason codes, and duplicates are removed.
- **Budget:** call count ≤ budget, stops exactly at the limit, cache hits are free, and rejected prospects are never enriched.
- **Scoring:** results are deterministic, and the tier boundaries are correct.
- **Outreach:** drafts are written only for tiers A and B, and every fact they mention appears in the record.
- **Failure isolation:** one failed call doesn't stop the run.
- **Stats:** the funnel numbers add up (sourced = valid + rejected).
- **Cancellation:** abort and timeout work.
- **`parseIcpForm`.**

**No-network guard:** stub the global `fetch` to throw, so any test that accidentally hits the network fails.

**Setup work:**
- The `@/` import alias needs a Vitest config, or the core can use relative imports.
- Nothing the tests import should import `server-only`.

## 8. Decisions that wait on the shared types

- **Prospect shape:** a company, a person, or a company plus a contact. This affects nearly every type.
- **Where prospects come from:** Crustdata search, an uploaded CSV, or fixtures only.
- **Enrichment fields** and the list of signals Crustdata actually returns.
- **The ID and duplicate key** format.
- **Score scale, tier thresholds,** and where the weights live.
- **Error model:** throw exceptions or return result objects, and the exact status values.
- **Observability:** does the pipeline emit events, or does observability code wrap the pipeline?
- **The cache:** where it lives and whether it persists between runs.
- **Who builds the real Crustdata client** and where `process.env` is read.

Until these are settled, I can still write `budget.ts`, the pipeline skeleton, the UI layout and `parseIcpForm` against draft interfaces.

## Questions to agree with your teammate

1. Is the unit we score a company, a person, or a company with a primary contact?
2. Where do candidate prospects come from for the demo: Crustdata search, an uploaded CSV, or fixtures?
3. Does the data layer own the Crustdata client and read `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` inside a `server-only` module, while tests always use fakes?
4. Which enrichment fields and signal types will `EnrichmentData` guarantee? Are all of them optional?
5. Should the agent receive cached data through an `EnrichmentCache` interface, or should the data provider cache on its own (hidden from the agent)? Should the cache persist between runs?
6. Should failures be thrown as errors or returned as result objects?
7. What does observability look like: `PipelineObserver.onEvent`, a logger interface, or both?
8. Should outreach be template-only, or use an LLM? An LLM needs a new key and dependency, and adds cost.
9. Should `zod` become a direct dependency for validating input and provider responses? `package.json` is shared.
10. Who owns the shared files: `vitest.config`, `package.json`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and the boilerplate SVGs in `public/`?
11. Should code import with `@/core/...` or relative paths? This depends on the Vitest alias setup.
12. What are the default and maximum enrichment budgets, and the quick-fit threshold?

I can also turn this plan into a shareable page for your teammate if that would help.

# SignalScout AI: revised plan

This is still planning only. I didn't modify any files or run any Git commands. The Next.js points below come from the docs bundled with the installed 16.4.0 version, which I read during the earlier steps.

## 0. Who owns which files

| Owner | Paths |
|---|---|
| **You** | `src/core/agent/**`, `src/app/**` (layout, page, actions, error page, `_components/`, `_lib/`) |
| **Teammate** | `src/core/types.ts`, `src/core/data/**` (the Crustdata client and the fixture provider), `src/core/fixtures/**`, `src/core/observability/**`, `tests/**` |
| **Shared: agree before anyone edits** | `package.json` and its lock file, `next.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`, a future `vitest.config.*`, `.gitignore`, `.env` and a future `.env.example`, `README.md`, `public/`, `scripts/` |
| **Leave alone** | `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. `next dev` manages the AGENTS.md block. |

**Two consequences:**
- I won't suggest touching `src/core/types.ts` until the contract in section 9 is agreed.
- A `src/proxy.ts` file would sit outside both of your areas. The docs also say Proxy shouldn't be used as a full authorization solution. So access control lives inside the Server Action instead (section 3).

**Splitting the types.** Only types that cross the boundary between the data layer and the agent go in the shared `types.ts`. Types that only the agent and the UI use stay in your own `src/core/agent/types.ts`. That keeps the shared contract small. Those agent-only types are:
- `IcpInput`
- `RunResult`
- `ScoredProspect`
- `OutreachDraft`
- `CostLedger`
- `StageFailure`

## 1. Scope for the first version

- **Data sources:** Crustdata for real data, and synthetic fixtures for development, tests and the public demo. No CSV import.
- **What we score:** companies (recommended). Crustdata company search plus company enrichment covers the ICP. Searching for people and contacts adds more paid operation types, so it waits. Outreach drafts are written to a target role (for example "Head of Sales at {company}") instead of a named person.
- **One complete run, then results.** The Server Action returns when the run finishes. Streaming progress comes later (section 7).
- **No LLM** (section 8).

## 2. Modules in `src/core/agent/`

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `index.ts` | Exports only `runPipeline` and the public types. |
| `types.ts` | The agent-only types listed in section 0. |
| `config.ts` | Default limits, the scoring weights, the freshness window for facts, and the cost table (section 4). |
| `pipeline.ts` | Runs the stages in order, applies the failure policy (section 6) and builds the `RunResult`. |
| `icp.ts` | Checks the ICP input and turns it into neutral `CompanySearchCriteria`. The data layer translates those criteria into Crustdata's filter syntax. |
| `source.ts` | Calls `searchCompanies` through the cost ledger. |
| `validate.ts` | Free checks: domain format, duplicates (by normalized domain), exclusion list, size and location limits, and a quick fit score. |
| `ledger.ts` | The cost ledger: reserve credits before a call, settle after it, and enforce all three limits. Pure code. |
| `enrich.ts` | Ranks prospects, checks the cache, calls `enrichCompany` through the ledger, and stops calling after repeated failures (a circuit breaker). |
| `score.ts` | Deterministic scoring, weighted by how reliable each piece of evidence is (section 5). |
| `outreach.ts` | Writes template-based drafts. Each sentence is linked to the facts it uses. |
| `claimGuard.ts` | Rejects any draft that states something as fact when the evidence doesn't support it. |

The core still doesn't read `process.env` or import `server-only`, so it can run in Vitest with no network.

## 3. Public access: synthetic by default, live mode controlled by the server

**Server Actions can be called by anyone.** The bundled data-security guide says a Server Action "is reachable via a direct POST request", and that authorization must be checked inside each one. So hiding the live-mode toggle in the UI protects nothing.

**How the server picks the mode:** `src/app/_lib/access.ts` (server-only) runs live mode only if all four of these are true:
1. A server-wide switch is on, for example `SIGNALSCOUT_LIVE_ENABLED=true`. It defaults to off.
2. `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` is present.
3. The person entered an operator access code in a form field (never in the URL), and it matches a server env var. The comparison uses a timing-safe check.
4. There's room left under the server-wide daily credit ceiling.

**Fail closed.** If any check fails, the server refuses the live request with a clear message. It never quietly falls back to synthetic data, because a synthetic result passed off as real would mislead.

**Rules that apply on every request:**
- The form's mode setting is only a request. The server decides the mode actually used.
- All limits come from the server. Any limit the user enters is clamped to the server's maximum.
- Only one live run at a time.
- Synthetic runs also have a prospect cap.
- No `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables. The key and the flags stay on the server. The docs note that non-`NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables are never put in the browser bundle.

**Known limitation.** The daily ceiling and the one-live-run lock are kept in memory, so they reset on restart and aren't shared across serverless instances. That's acceptable for a hackathon demo run by an operator. Making them durable comes later.

**New env vars mean editing `.env`, a shared file.** We'd also want a `.env.example` that documents them. Both need agreement.

## 4. Cost accounting

**Crustdata charges credits, and the cost varies by endpoint and by the fields requested.** Its docs say to confirm current costs in your dashboard. I couldn't find official per-call numbers, only third-party reports:

| Operation | Reported cost (an estimate) | Billed |
|---|---|---|
| `company_search` | about 1 credit per search; one reseller lists a per-result price | per call or per result (to be confirmed) |
| `company_enrich` | 1–4 credits per company, depending on fields | per company |
| `company_identify` | reportedly free | per call |

**The cost table** in `config.ts` has one entry per operation:
- how it's billed (per call or per result)
- the estimated credits
- the worst-case credits
- where the number came from: `estimate` or `dashboard_confirmed`

Live mode refuses to start if any operation it needs is still marked `estimate`, unless the operator explicitly accepts the estimates.

**Limits per run:**
- `maxSearchCalls`, for example 1
- `maxEnrichCalls`, for example 10
- `maxTotalCredits`

The server-wide daily credit ceiling sits on top of these.

**Reserve, then settle:**
1. **Before a call:** reserve the worst-case cost. If that would break any limit, the call is skipped and logged as `skipped_budget`. It never throws.
2. **After the call:** record the actual cost if the response reports one (open question for your teammate). Otherwise record the estimate and mark the entry as estimated.
3. **When a call fails:** it still counts toward the call limit. Its credits are released only if we know Crustdata didn't charge; the default is to keep the charge.
4. **Cache hits** cost 0 and are logged separately.

**Synthetic mode runs the same ledger** with the same cost table. The UI can then show "this run would have cost about X credits". That's useful for the demo, and it exercises the accounting code in tests.

**Other ways to keep costs down:**
- Free validation and duplicate removal happen before any paid call.
- Only the top K companies are enriched.
- At most one enrichment call per domain per run.
- Only the fields scoring uses are requested, if Crustdata lets us choose fields.
- About 3 calls run at once, each with a timeout.
- At most one retry, and it's charged.

## 5. Evidence model

**Each important company fact is stored with where it came from** (proposed shape for the shared contract):

```
Fact<T> {
  value: T
  source: { provider: 'crustdata' | 'fixture' | 'derived' | 'user_input',
            operation?, retrievedAt, sourceUrl? }
  status: 'verified' | 'reported' | 'inferred' | 'stale' | 'conflicting'
  asOf?                      // the date the fact describes, as opposed to when we fetched it
  derivedFrom?: FactRef[]    // filled in for inferred facts
}
```

**The five statuses:**

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verified` | Confirmed by an exact identifier match, for example a domain that maps to the company. In the first version this applies to identity facts only. |
| `reported` | Returned by Crustdata during this run, or from a cache entry still inside the freshness window. Not independently checked. |
| `inferred` | Calculated by our own code, for example "growing" worked out from a change in headcount. |
| `stale` | Older than the freshness window. |
| `conflicting` | Sources disagree. |

**What outreach may do with each status** (enforced by `claimGuard.ts`):

| Status | Plain statement | Hedged wording | Shown in the UI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verified` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `reported` | ❌ | ✅ ("it looks like…") | ✅ |
| `inferred`, `stale`, `conflicting` | ❌ | ❌ | ✅, with a label |

**How it's enforced.** Each template sentence states the lowest status it accepts. Each draft records `claims[]`, which links every sentence to the IDs of the facts it uses. Any draft that breaks the rules is dropped, and the reason is recorded against that prospect. Because the templates are deterministic, the guard can be tested exhaustively.

**Scoring uses the same evidence.** Weaker facts lower the weight and confidence of the criteria that depend on them, and the score breakdown shows the evidence used.

## 6. Failure model

**Prospect-level problems are recorded, and the run continues.** Each is stored as a `ProspectIssue { prospectId, stage, code, retryable }`:
- an invalid or duplicate record
- enrichment returning nothing (`not_found`)
- a timeout or one-off error for a single company
- one malformed field
- a draft rejected by the claim guard

**A budget skip is not a failure.** It's a status: `skipped_budget` or `skipped_low_fit`.

**Stage-level problems** are stored as a `StageFailure { stage, code, effect }`. `effect` is either `run_stopped` or `stage_stopped_continue_degraded`.

| Problem | What happens |
|---|---|
| Invalid ICP input, live access refused, or a needed operation missing from the cost table | `run_stopped` before any paid call |
| Search fails as a whole (authentication error, out of credits, provider down, response doesn't match the contract) | `run_stopped`; there's nothing to process |
| Enrichment fails across the board: authentication error, out of credits, rate limits beyond a threshold, or about 3 failures in a row | Stop making enrichment calls (`stage_stopped_continue_degraded`). Scoring continues using unenriched data, marked low confidence. Outreach only covers prospects whose required facts exist. |
| The ledger is inconsistent, or the cost of an operation is unknown | Stop all paid calls (fail closed) |
| A bug throws inside scoring or outreach | That stage fails, and the result returns whatever was completed |

**Overall run status:** `RunResult.status` is `completed`, `completed_with_issues` or `stopped`. The UI shows stage failures as a banner and prospect issues inline.

**The data layer has to classify provider errors** for this to work. The codes are:
- prospect-level: `not_found`, `timeout`, `invalid_response`
- systemic: `auth`, `insufficient_credits`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`

## 7. UI and how it calls the pipeline (first version)

**Flow:**
1. `IcpForm` → `useActionState(runSignalScout)`.
2. The action checks the input on the server.
3. `access.ts` decides the mode actually used.
4. `deps.ts` builds the fixture provider or the Crustdata provider.
5. The action calls `runPipeline`.
6. It returns `toRunView(result)`: a trimmed, serializable view.

**Next.js setup:**
- `page.tsx` sets `export const maxDuration = 60`; the docs say a page-level setting applies to its Server Actions.
- While the run is in progress, the form shows a pending state with the button disabled.
- No `use cache` and no Cache Components: each run is triggered by a user and should produce fresh results.

**Components:**
- `IcpForm`: a synthetic/live selector, plus an access-code field that only matters for live mode.
- `RunSummary`: the funnel counts and the overall status.
- `CostPanel`: credits used, estimated and saved, for each operation type and limit.
- `ProspectTable` with expandable `ScoreBreakdown` rows.
- `EvidenceBadge`: the source and status of a fact.
- `OutreachDraft`: shows which facts each sentence uses, with a copy button.
- `IssuesList`: the failure banner and per-prospect issues.

**Later:** stage-by-stage progress through a streaming Route Handler. The first version doesn't need it, because the caps keep runs short.

## 8. Role of an LLM in the first version

**None.** ICP input comes from a structured form, scoring is rule-based, and outreach uses deterministic templates. The reasons:
- There's no LLM dependency or key in the repo.
- Every model call would cost money.
- The claim guard can only be enforced reliably on output we can predict.
- Fixture-based tests stay deterministic.

**`OutreachWriter` stays an interface,** so an LLM writer can be added later. That would need an explicit decision first, and it would have to:
- pass the same claim guard
- run only in authorized live mode
- have its own line and limit in the ledger
- add its dependency through `package.json`, which is shared

## 9. Decisions that block implementation

The smallest set to agree before `types.ts` is written:

1. **The unit we score and its duplicate key.** Proposed: a company, keyed by normalized domain.
2. **The minimum `CompanyRecord` fields.** Proposed: name, domain, industry, headcount, headcount growth, country, funding stage and date, plus a short list of signals. Each one wrapped in `Fact<T>`.
3. **The `Fact<T>` shape** and the five evidence statuses.
4. **The provider interfaces.** Proposed:
   - `searchCompanies(criteria, { limit, signal })`
   - `enrichCompany(domain, { signal })`

   The fixture provider implements exactly the same interfaces.
5. **The neutral `CompanySearchCriteria`** that the agent produces and the data layer translates into Crustdata filters.
6. **Call metadata and error codes:** `ProviderCallMeta { operation, creditsCharged? }` and the error codes from section 6.
7. **The list of operation names, and who owns cost numbers.** Proposed: the data layer reports actual costs when Crustdata provides them; the agent owns the estimates and the limits.

**These can wait:**
- the observability interface (the pipeline accepts an optional observer)
- persistent caching
- scoring weights and tier thresholds
- the details of `RunResult` (agent-owned)
- contacts and people data
- streaming
- an LLM

## Questions for your teammate

1. Do you agree that the unit we score is a company, keyed by domain (decision 1)?
2. Which Crustdata endpoints and versions will the data layer call? Do responses report the credits charged?
3. Is search billed per call or per result? What do enrichment fields cost on our plan? Please confirm in the dashboard.
4. Can the data layer classify every provider error into the agreed codes?
5. Where is the cache, and what is the freshness window for `reported` facts?
6. Shared files: who adds the new env vars and `.env.example`, and who owns `vitest.config` and `README.md`?
7. Do we avoid new dependencies in the first version? That means checking input by hand instead of making `zod` a direct dependency.

## Recommended implementation order

1. **Agree the 7 blocking decisions.** Your teammate then writes `types.ts` and stubs a fixture provider. Meanwhile you build work that doesn't depend on the contract:
   - the `src/app` shell: metadata, page layout, an empty results area
   - `IcpInput` and form parsing
   - the logic of `access.ts`
2. **`ledger.ts` and `config.ts`.** Depends only on decision 7.
3. **After `types.ts` exists:** `icp.ts`, `validate.ts`, `enrich.ts` with the circuit breaker, `score.ts`, `outreach.ts` with `claimGuard.ts`, then `pipeline.ts`.
4. **Connect the Server Action to the fixture provider.** A full synthetic run then works end to end.
5. **Results UI:** summary, cost panel, table, evidence badges, drafts, issues.
6. **Live mode.** Wire up the access checks and your teammate's Crustdata provider. Confirm costs in the dashboard, then do one manual live run with tiny caps (1 search, 2 enrichments).
7. **Hardening, plus demo notes in the README** (a shared file, so agree first).
8. **Later:** streaming progress, persistent run storage, contacts, an optional LLM writer.

I can turn this into a shareable page for your teammate if that would help.

**Sources:**
- [Crustdata pricing docs](https://docs.crustdata.com/general/pricing)
- [Crustdata pricing docs (markdown)](https://docs.crustdata.com/general/pricing.md)
- [hackceleration: Crustdata Claude connector](https://hackceleration.com/resources/integrations/claude/crustdata)

content.text:
I built the SignalScout AI shell and ICP form in `src/app/`. It passes the type-check, lint and production build, and I tested it in the browser. All changes are inside `src/app/`; I didn't touch any teammate files, `src/core/types.ts`, `package.json`, `.env` or other config, didn't write a Crustdata client, made no API calls, and didn't commit or push.

**One thing to check:** to restart the server during testing I ran `taskkill /F /IM node.exe`. That force-stopped **every** Node process on your machine, not just my server. If you had a dev server, editor tooling or another Node app running then, it was killed and needs restarting. I stopped my server the second time by its port only.

## Repository status

Before I started, the working tree was clean on `main`, at commit `e9853b3 Rename package to signalscout`.

## Files changed

**Modified:**
- `src/app/layout.tsx`: SignalScout AI title and description, plus a header and footer.
- `src/app/page.tsx`: replaced the starter page.
- `src/app/globals.css`: colour tokens, and removed the Arial override so the Geist font applies.

**New, top level:**
- `src/app/actions.ts`: the Server Action `submitIcp`. It checks the form on the server and only shows the profile back; nothing is called.
- `src/app/error.tsx`: the error page.
- `src/app/_lib/icp-form.ts`: the form's own types, options, and the reading and checking logic. It's deliberately not the shared contract.

**New, `src/app/_components/`:**
- `AppHeader.tsx`
- `IcpForm.tsx`
- `ProspectWorkspace.tsx`: the only client component; it holds the form state for both the form and the results.
- `form/`: `FormField`, `TextField`, `TextAreaField`, `SelectField`, `DataModeSelector`
- `results/`: `ResultsPanel`, `Panel` (a reusable card with an empty state and loading bars), `StatTile`, `IcpSummary`, `ProspectScoresPlaceholder`, `EvidencePlaceholder`, `BudgetUsagePlaceholder`, `OutreachDraftsPlaceholder`

## How it behaves

- **Fields:** industry and company size are required. Location, keywords and excluded domains are optional and take commas or new lines.
- **Cleanup:** duplicate entries are removed, and pasted URLs become bare domains, so `https://www.Acme.com/about` becomes `acme.com`.
- **Data mode:** synthetic is the default and the only option you can pick. Live Crustdata is shown but disabled. The server also rejects a live request, and I confirmed that by enabling the radio in the browser and submitting.
- **Results area:** shows placeholders for scores, evidence, budget usage and outreach drafts. After a valid submit it shows the accepted profile and says the pipeline isn't connected yet.

## Following the bundled Next.js 16.4 docs

- The form uses `useActionState`, and errors are returned as values instead of thrown.
- `metadata` stays in a Server Component, and `title.template` has the `default` it requires.
- `error.tsx` uses the `retry` prop (stable since 16.3) rather than the older `reset`.

## Bug found and fixed in testing

After a submit, the company-size dropdown went back to its placeholder. React only applies a dropdown's default value when it first mounts, so I now remount that one field whenever its value changes. Retesting confirmed the value is kept.

## Run and verify locally

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000, then:

1. Click **Find prospects** with the form empty. You should see "Enter a target industry" and "Choose a company size".
2. Enter `not a domain` in Excluded domains. It's flagged, and your other entries stay filled in.
3. Enter valid values, such as `Fintech`, `51–200`, `United Kingdom, Germany`, and `https://www.competitor.com/x`. The results area shows the cleaned profile.
4. Resize the window. At desktop width the form and results sit side by side; at phone width they stack, with no sideways scrolling.
